reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Spherocytes plus negative Coombs plus family history means hereditary spherocytosis
Heinz bodies and bite cells during oxidant crisis mean G6PD deficiency
Do not assay G6PD during acute crisis; reticulocytes falsely normalise it
PNH triad: haemolysis, thrombosis and marrow failure from lost CD55 CD59
reference.pathophysiology: Membrane cytoskeleton defects shed surface area until cells sphere and fail splenic slits, while red cell enzyme defects either starve ATP pumps (pyruvate kinase) or exhaust glutathione antioxidant defence (G6PD) under oxidant load. Complement regulator loss in PNH exposes cells to membrane attack complex lysis inside vessels.
additionalDifferentials: Spherocytosis versus autoimmune spherocyte haemolysis by Coombs
G6PD episodic versus pyruvate kinase chronic haemolysis
additionalInvestigations: Blood film with reticulocytes, LDH, bilirubin and haptoglobin
Direct antiglobulin test on every new haemolysis
Osmotic fragility or EMA binding for spherocytosis; G6PD assay timed outside crisis
